{{Quote|You are trespassers&mdash;intruders, spies. Worse of all, you are Human. Humans have always tried to destroy what alien species have built.|[[Nolaa Tarkona]]|<ref name="JB">''[[Young Jedi Knights: Jedi Bounty]]''</ref>}}
'''Humans''', taxonomically referred to as '''''Homo sapiens''''', were [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] most numerous and [[Politics/Legends|politically]] dominant [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] with millions of major and minor [[Colonies/Legends|colonies]] galaxywide. Believed to have originated on the galactic capital of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], they could be found anywhere, engaged in many different pursuits: [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]], [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]], [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]], [[Merchant/Legends|merchants]], [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]], [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]], [[Farm/Legends|farmers]], [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lords]], laborers, [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]], [[Slaver/Legends|slavers]], and many others, including [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and [[Sith/Legends|Sith]]. Since Humans were the most common sentient species, they were often considered to be a standard or average to which the biology, psychology, and culture of other species were compared.

==Biology and appearance==
===Physiology===
{{Quote|Well let's have a look at you. Hmm. Biped. More or less symmetrical. Far less hair than the last one. Opposable digits. Mostly water hey?|[[Unidentified Rakatan prisoner|Ancient Rakatan prisoner]], upon meeting the Human [[Revan/Legends|Revan]]|translated=1|<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Human_NEGAS.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Humans were four-limbed bipeds with a bilateral symmetry]]
The Humans were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] that belonged to the [[Primate/Legends|simians]], a subgroup<ref name="LCFO" /> of the [[Primate/Legends|primate]]<ref name="Blog">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-the-celestials|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut &mdash; The Celestials|int=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut}}</ref> order of [[Mammal/Legends|mammals]].<ref name="LCFO" /> As such, they were similar to a number of other species variously designated as [[Ape/Legends|apes]], including the sentient [[Ma'alkerrite ape-man]].<ref name="Blurb">''[[The Lost Jedi Adventure Game Book]]'', Front matter</ref> They were taxonomically referred to as ''Homo sapiens''.<ref name="ff56">{{FactFile|56|OUT 1-2|Outer Rim Worlds}}</ref>

Humans were bipedal beings with a bilateral symmetry, having a front and a back end, as well as an upside and downside. Their body comprised a head, neck, torso, and four [[Limb/Legends|limbs]]. The upper limbs, called arms, ended in hands which had five fingers each; the lower ones, called legs, ended in feet with also five digits. The Human fingers had multiple points of articulation, and one of them was an opposable thumb that allowed for fine manipulation. Finally, they had one head perched atop a torso.<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> Other sentient species that had a body type roughly similar to Humans and walked upright were often referred to as [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]], since Humans were the most common example.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Unlike other mammalian species such as [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiees]] or [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]], they had only a light covering of body [[Hair/Legends|hair]]. Most of it was concentrated on the head and, in the case of adult males, face.<ref name="AE">''[[Alien Encounters]]''</ref>

Humans were endotherms, or "warm-[[Blood/Legends|blooded]]" animals, meaning they maintained a constant body [[Temperature/Legends|temperature]] independent of the environment using the energy from their food.<ref name="SWSA">''[[Star Wars Science Adventures: Journey Across Planet X]]''</ref> While some mistakenly described themselves as [[Diet/Legends|carnivores]],<ref name="TDT">{{StoryCite|story=Empire Blues: The Devaronian's Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref> Humans were in fact omnivores, subsisting on both animal tissue and [[Plant/Legends|plant]]-based [[Foodstuff/Legends|foods]].<ref name="JJTM">''[[Star Wars Episode I: Junior Jedi Training Manual]]''</ref> For that reason, their gastrointestinal system was much longer than that of true carnivores such as the [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronians]].<ref name="TDT" /> Many Humans were partial to food products that were unhealthy for them because of their high fat or [[Sugar/Legends|sugar]] content.<ref name="JJTM" />

The Human genome was considered to be remarkably elastic. In reaction to environmental changes, selection pressures only needed few millennia to engage new genes and reshape the Human bodies. A consequence of that exceptional adaptability was the existence of many [[Near-Human]] species&mdash;that is offshoots of the baseline Humans who had followed their own evolution.<ref name="EGW cut7">{{SW|url=news/the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-part-7-the-grand-army-of-the-republic|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 7 &mdash; The Grand Army of the Republic}}</ref> Such offshoots included the [[Stennes Shifter/Legends|Stennes Shifters]],<ref name="SWC ">''[[Star Wars Chronicles]]''</ref> the scaly-skinned [[Zisian]]s,<ref name="The Paradise Snare">''[[The Paradise Snare]]''</ref> the blue-skinned [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]]<ref name="UAA">''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]''</ref> and the gaunt [[Pau'an/Legends|Pau'ans]].<ref name="NEGAS" />

As was common to many humanoid species, Humans included [[Gender/Legends|males and females]]&mdash;many females had relatively more pronounced [[Breast/Legends|breasts]], smaller stature, and lesser quantity of body hair.<ref name="RPGRCR" /> Members of the Human race could [[Hybrid/Legends|interbreed]] naturally with many other species, including the [[Epicanthix]], [[Echani/Legends|Echani]],<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref> the [[Ferroan]],<ref name="RP">''[[Rogue Planet]]''</ref> [[Hamadryas]],<ref name="Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref> the [[Kiffar/Legends|Kiffar]],<ref name="Legacy of the Force: Bloodlines">''[[Legacy of the Force: Bloodlines]]''</ref> the [[Miraluka/Legends|Miraluka]],<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic Handbook">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic Handbook]]''</ref> the [[Nagai/Legends|Nagai]],<ref name="The Forgotten War: The Nagai and the Tofs">{{Hyperspace|url=fans/hyperspace/source/nagai11202009/index.html|text=The Forgotten War: The Nagai and the Tofs|int=The Forgotten War: The Nagai and the Tofs}}</ref> and the [[Theelin/Legends|Theelin]].<ref name="The Essential Guide to Characters">''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> Most of the aforementioned species were in fact Near-Humans. In some cases, Humans could only produce offsprings with members of other species with the help of genetic manipulation or [[Sith alchemy/Legends|alchemy]]. Examples of those include the [[Sith (species)/Legends|Red Sith]],<ref name="NEGC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> the [[Qiraash/Legends|Qiraash]] or the [[Umbaran/Legends|Umbarans]].<ref name="CNII">''[[Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows]]''</ref>

===Physical diversity===
{{Quote|Selection pressures need a few millennia at most to engage new genes and reshape their bodies in response to environmental changes, as the galaxy's countless near-human populations attest.|[[Hali Ke]]|<ref name="Blog" />}}
[[File:Senator_Bana_Breemu.jpg|thumb|150px|A Human [[Gender/Legends|female]] displaying characteristic curves and hairless face.]]
Despite overall physiological uniformity, baseline Humans varied greatly in appearance,<ref name="RPGRCR" /> and no two Humans looked exactly alike.<ref name="Sony">{{SonyCite|url=players/guides.vm?id=70000|text=Character Creation Guide}}</ref> One of the diversity factors was height. Humans averaged 1.70 to 1.80 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in height, although males were usually taller and heavier than females.<ref name="RPGRCR" /> Some individuals affected by [[giantism]] could grow up to 2.30 meters. On the contrary, those afflicted with [[nanism]] could be as small-sized as 1.3 meters.<ref name="PLH">{{PolyhedronCite|103|Prophets of the Dark Side: Villains for the Star Wars: New Republic Campaign, Part One}}</ref>

Their hair was grown, cut, and styled for aesthetic or ritualistic reasons&mdash;as with the elaborate hairstyles of the [[Royal House of Naboo/Legends|Royal Naboo]] and the traditional braids of Human [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawans]].<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref> The facial hair grown by adult males could be grown, styled, or shaved completely.<ref name="Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith">{{Film|III}}</ref> Their hair color ranged from blond to black, sometimes with hues of red or brown, changing to gray or white as [[Standard year/Legends|years]] passed. It could be straight, wavy, or curly. In addition to those varied hair colors, their [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] came in shades of blue, green, gray, or brown. Gradiation of skin tone was also seen among baseline Humans, usually limited to various shades of brown,<ref name="RPGRCR" /> ranging from dark brown,<ref name="ESB">As exemplified by [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] in {{Film|V}}.</ref> through lighter shades,<ref name="Bana">As exemplified by [[Bana Breemu/Legends|Bana Breemu]] in {{Film|III}}.</ref> to pale skin.<ref name="Luke">As exemplified by [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]</ref>

There existed a classification of Human beings in use at the [[Fusai/Legends|Fusai]] [[Fusai library|library branch]] of the [[Celebratus Archive]], which cataloged Humans by degrees. In that system, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]<ref name="TCA">"[[The Constancia Affair]]"</ref> and [[Gyla Petro]] were referred to as "10th Degree" Humans.<ref name="TKD">"[[The Kashyyyk Depths]]"</ref>

===Life cycle===
{{Quote|Mother Rell is nearly three hundred years old, but her spirit is so strong that it will not let her body die.|[[Augwynne Djo]], about her centuries-old mother|<ref name="CoPL">''[[The Courtship of Princess Leia]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Dookus_face.png|thumb|left|200px|An 80-year-old male Human displaying several signs of aging, such as white hair, wrinkles, and slightly sagging skin.]]
Humans [[Reproduction/Legends|reproduced]] sexually, with offsprings being produced by the fusion of [[sperm]] and [[Ovum|ova]]. The fetus typically developed in the womb of their mother, who had a distinctive shape accompanied by a significant weight gain during the process.<ref name="HttE">''[[Heir to the Empire]]''</ref> Being mammals, Humans gave birth to live [[Youngling/Legends|young]], either one or several at a time.<ref name="Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith" /> Two children born at the same birth were referred to as [[Twin/Legends|twins]], and three as triplets.<ref name="Tripl">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20040122threat|text=Triplet Threat|int=Triplet Threat}}</ref> The delivery itself normally took place after nine [[Standard month/Legends|months]] of pregnancy. It was a painful process that could take as much as ten [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]].<ref name="LC">''[[The Last Command]]''</ref> In some circumstances, the mother could [[Death/Legends|die]] during childbirth, although it rarely happened on worlds that had top-flight medical technologies.<ref name="ROSn">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref> During their first months of existence, Human babies were usually fed with [[Milk/Legends|milk]] from their mother's breasts.<ref name="SBS">''[[The New Jedi Order: Star by Star]]''</ref>

The period during which a young Human developed from a child into an adult was known as adolescence. According to the [[Equani]] therapist [[Klo Merit]], that stage of development was hard to endure without support.<ref name="MS2">''[[MedStar II: Jedi Healer]]''</ref> Regardless of physiological and psychological changes, the [[Age of responsibility|legal transition]] from childhood to adulthood depended on culture. Usually humans are considered adults since 14.<ref name="Plagueis">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>

Typically, Humans had an average lifespan of 100<ref name="sagarulebook">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Saga Edition Core Rulebook]]''</ref> to 120 standard years. Those who were [[Force-sensitive/Legends|keenly atuned]] to [[The Force/Legends|the Force]],<ref name="NEGAS" /> a ubiquitous and binding power that suffused the whole [[Universe/Legends|Known Universe]],<ref name="AGTSWU2">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref> could live up to 200.<ref name="NEGAS" /> On worlds that possessed advanced technology, such as [[Bakura/Legends|Bakura]], individuals over the age of 160 who were still hale and hearty were not unheard of. By [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]], the Human couple [[Eppie Belden|Eppie]] and [[Orn Belden]] were respectively 132 and 164, although the latter wore a voice amplifier on his chest and had gone through three hearts in his life.<ref name="TTaB">''[[The Truce at Bakura]]''</ref> Thanks to countless medical treatments and organ transplants accessible to a financial elite, it was possible to extend Human lifetime to the age of 300,<ref name="CTP">''[[Star Wars Chronicles: The Prequels]]''</ref> and at least one Forceful [[Shayoto|individual]] was known to have reached the age of 800. In spite of his age, that individual, the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Shayoto]], was still able to hike all the way up [[Mount Meru (Deneba)|Mount Meru]] with a [[Cane/Legends|cane]].<ref name="darklords3">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 3|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 3]]</ref> At any rate, individuals past the age of 80 were considered old,<ref name="ROJN">[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'' novel]]</ref> and most Humans still died in their early hundreds unless they were wealthy enough to afford rejuvenation procedures of the sort available at [[Aurora Medical Facility]] on [[Obroa-skai/Legends|Obroa-skai]].<ref name="MFn">[[Millennium Falcon (novel)|''Millennium Falcon'']]</ref> However, many older Humans were still healthy enough to pursue very active careers, as exemplified by [[Gilad Pellaeon/Legends|Gilad Pellaeon]], who still served as the supreme commander of the [[Galactic Alliance Defense Force]] in [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], at age 91.<ref name="Betrayal">''[[Legacy of the Force: Betrayal]]''</ref> Natural signs of ageing in Humans included the whitening or fall of the hair, the loss of teeth, appearance of deep lines, wrinkles and dark blemishes on the skin. Old Humans would experience a decline in many cognitive processes,<ref name="TTaB" /> frequently losing track of [[Time/Legends|time]], misidentifying people or places,<ref name="CoPL" /> and, in extreme cases, momentarily forgetting about their own identity or state.<ref name="TTaB" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|Humans are simultaneously capable of extraordinary viciousness and extraordinary acts of kindness and altruism.|Hali Ke|<ref name="Blog" />}}
Humans were noted for being naturally learning and extremely adaptable&mdash;not only in terms of physiology, but also mentality and society. Their societies were capable of transforming very quickly in response to a wide array of conditions, which explains why two Human populations could have next to nothing in common culturally speaking. As noted by the [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoan]] scientist [[Hali Ke]], some Human peoples had more in common with neighbors of other species than with their own kind.<ref name="EGW cut7" />

==History==
===Origin===
{{Quote|I was saying that, among the intelligent species of the galaxy, we humans are a most prolific, preternaturally protean people.|[[Duttes Mer]]|<ref name="Mindharp">''[[Lando Calrissian and the Mindharp of Sharu]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Baby_leia.png|thumb|left|250px|A Human newborn.]]
Having a recorded and civilized history reaching back far beyond the beginning of space travel,<ref name="NEC" /> their original homeworld forgotten, and early history of Humans was lost to their scientists in the depths of millennia. Whatever the original homeworld was, it was nearly universally accepted that Humans evolved on one of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] near the galaxy's center (though there were few who believed that the homeworld no longer existed or was beyond the bounds of known space). Unfortunately, most of the Core World civilizations were as old as Human collective memory, and there was no conclusive record of one single homeworld.<ref name=":0">[[Into the Core Worlds|''Into the Core Worlds'']]</ref> Humans were among the few sentient species in the galaxy whose homeworld was unknown, the [[Ryn/Legends|Ryn]], [[Yoda's species/Legends|Yoda's species]] and the [[Baragwin/Legends|Baragwins]] being some other examples.

According to an inscription found by [[Archaeology/Legends|archaeologists]] Dr. [[Ualp Xathan]] and [[Fem Nu-Ar]] on [[Seoul 5]] around [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], the cradle of Human civilization was the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] Notron,<ref name="SW84" /> an archaic name for [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].<ref name="NEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> This claim was shared with at least half a dozen other planets that believed they were the origin point of humanity.<ref name="SW84" /> The ancient [[Zhell/Legends|Zhell]] nations, who drove the [[Near-Human]] [[Taung/Legends|Taungs]] from Coruscant, may have been the progenitors of later Humans.<ref name="NEC" /> Coruscant's ground had been several kilometers below its inhabitants' feet for millennia, with the lowest depths of its planet-wide city dating back to [[100,000 BBY/Legends|100,000 BBY]]. Thus, it was impossible to carry out the historical study and archaeological research on the planet's prehistory necessary to prove or to disprove that theory. In addition, Coruscant's natural climate was said to be too cold to support Human life,<ref name="The Essential Guide to Planets and Moons">''[[The Essential Guide to Planets and Moons]]''</ref> a claim difficult to be reconciled with the theory that it was the original Human homeworld. [[Tarnese Bleyd]] believed that the ancestors of Humans favored trees and high ground based upon his observations of human hunting behavior.<ref name="MedStar I: Battle Surgeons">''[[MedStar I: Battle Surgeons]]''</ref> Entire crusades and civil wars were devoted to the question of the origin point of Humans among worlds competing for the title, as well as many academic careers. At least by the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], no Core world had managed to produce an undisputed archaeological or fossil record to prove that it had once hosted the original pre-space Human civilization.<ref name=":0" />   

It is possible that some ancient civilization, such as the [[Celestial/Legends|Celestials]] or even the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]], transported early Humans from their original home planet to others. It was, in fact, alleged that they had once been a slave race of the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]];<ref name="NEC" /> however, any knowledge of Human enslavement was absent from a Rakatan [[Overseer (droid)|overseer droid's]] records<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic" /> as of [[3956 BBY]].<ref name="kotordate">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' established that the events of ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'' happenend in [[3956 BBY]].</ref> Some of the far-flung 'colonies' eventually diverged genetically from the Human baseline, giving rise to various Near-Human races and species.

During the [[Jedi Civil War]], the Jedi [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] discovered evidence in the oral traditions of the [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Sand People]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] that the human species may have originated as slaves taken from that planet by the Rakata, the Sand People being the genetically distinct species that evolved from those who were left behind. The fact that the Sand People's legends indicated that the planet had once been far more temperate and habitable before an ancient war with the Rakata adds credence to this possibility. However, millennia of distortion introduced into the historical record combined with the Sand People's extreme hostility to the idea of introducing new interpretations into their oral tradition made it impossible for Revan to investigate this further.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref>

===Expansion===
[[File:GavJoriDaragon.jpg|thumb|right|200px|[[Daragon family|Two siblings]], male and female during the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]].]]
{{Quote|I studied the histories of your own scattered species, and I came to be fascinated with this concept, ''adventure''. Of all the races who gamble their well-being on uncertain returns&mdash;and there aren't that many, statistically&mdash;the trait's most noticeable in humans, one of the most successful life forms.|[[S. V. Skynx/Legends|S. V. Skynx]], to [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]|<ref name="The Lost Legacy">''[[Han Solo and the Lost Legacy]]''</ref>}}
The earliest legend concerning humans was the thirteen human [[Nations of Zhell]] that were involved in the [[Zhell–Taung war]], winning Coruscant over the [[Taung/Legends|Taung]] species.<ref name="NEA" />

Humans discovered space travel themselves, early in their history; in fact, they were already present on a few scattered colony planets of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] even before the development of [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]], thanks to the use of [[Sleeper ship/Legends|sleeper ships]]. Coruscant had grown to a [[Ecumenopolis/Legends|planet-wide city]] and, even during the centuries the planet was enslaved by the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakatan]] [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]], sleeper ships spread humanity to such Core Worlds as [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], [[Alsakan/Legends|Alsakan]], [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]], [[Chandrila/Legends|Chandrila]], [[Corulag/Legends|Corulag]], [[Csilla/Legends|Csilla]] (where they evolved into the near-Human [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]]) and [[Metellos/Legends|Metellos]].<ref name="NEC" /><ref name="NEA" />

Though some sources indicate that early humans were enslaved workers on Rakatan projects such as the [[Star Forge]],<ref name="NEC" /> the fact that the Rakatan [[Overseer (droid)|overseer droid]] in the [[Rakatan ruins (Dantooine)|Rakatan ruins]] on [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]] dating from that era did not recognize the Human species points to the contrary.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic" />

After the fall of the Infinite Empire circa [[25,200 BBY]], the Humans of the Core used Rakatan technology to set up a true interstellar civilization. At first, a network of [[hyperspace cannon]]s linked Coruscant with other Human-populated worlds, as well as the [[Duros/Legends|Duros]] civilization. [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] Humans were one of the first societies to develop [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] [[Starship/Legends|starships]] sometime before [[25,053 BBY]], spreading the technology to other Core Worlds. With the hyperdrive, their [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] and explorers traveled and met with other species, in a time known as the [[Expansionist Period/Legends|Expansionist Era]].<ref name="NEC" />

The Human colonies, which had expanded through the Core Worlds through slower-than-light travel, later established daughter colonies of their own in what became the [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]] region. During the last [[Pre-Republic era|pre-Republic]] years, Humans reached the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] and populated planets as far away as the [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]]. The [[Tionese (group)/Legends|Tionese]] warlord [[Xim/Legends|Xim the Despot]], whose conquests reached from the [[Cronese Sweeps]] to the [[Si'Klaata Cluster/Legends|Si'Klaata Cluster]] at the edge of [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]], was one of the most prominent Humans of the pre-Republic period.<ref name="NEC" />

===The Republic===
[[File:Human_Mercenary.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A Human [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]]]]

During the Expansionist Era, Humans began to play a dominant role in the development of the galaxy and in galactic politics. These Humans were eventually responsible for the [[Unification Wars (Galactic Republic)|Unification Wars]], which resulted from their expansionistic views. The wars themselves led to the formation of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], a galaxy-spanning affiliation of worlds and species. Though the Republic had many member species, most of the Republic's political, military, and economic leaders were Humans. Humans also made up a large proportion of the Jedi Order, and eventually came to dominate the Jedi's constant enemies, the [[Sith/Legends|Sith Order]]. By the end of the [[Old Sith Wars]], Humans also made up the majority of the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] warrior culture.<ref name="The History of the Mandalorians">{{InsiderCite|80|The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors}}</ref>

Most Humans under the Republic lived on predominantly Human worlds, although many Humans lived alongside [[Alien/Legends|aliens]] on their homeworlds, or together with several other species. Humans were more likely to live among nonhumans on the cosmopolitan Core Worlds, or on frontier worlds at the Outer Rim of the galaxy such as [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. Predominantly Human worlds outside of the Core included [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]], [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], [[Socorro/Legends|Socorro]], and [[Bakura/Legends|Bakura]].

Human population levels and significance inevitably led to a [[Humanocentrism|Humanocentric]] galaxy. Humanocentrism was pervasive and in many cases, subconscious. Humanocentrism was the source for the Human use of the term "[[Alien/Legends|alien]]" to describe nonhuman species. In some cases, this led to overt and even violent outbreaks of [[speciesism]]. Although explicit Humanocentrism was outlawed by the [[Rights of Sentience]] clause of the [[Galactic Constitution/Legends|Galactic Constitution]], Human-led companies such as [[Czerka Arms/Legends|Czerka]] [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] entire nonhuman species, while planets such as [[Taris/Legends|Taris]] reserved the best sections of the world for Humans and forced nonhumans into ghettos. The majority of slaves in the galaxy were nonhumans.

At the end of the Galactic Republic's history, the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] worsened relationships between Humans and aliens, since the Republic was led by Humans while the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] was led by aliens. This was evident by the formation of several pro-Human groups within the Republic, including the [[Commission for the Protection of the Republic/Legends|Commission for the Protection of the Republic]] (COMPOR) and its chapter [[SAGroup (COMPOR)/Legends|SAGroup]]. COMPOR pressured the First Minister of the [[Coruscant Ministry of Ingress/Legends|Coruscant Ministry of Ingress]], [[Tannon Praji/Legends|Tannon Praji]], into deporting all members of species whose homeworld had joined the CIS, thus decreasing the nonhuman presence in the Galactic capital.

===Galactic Empire===
{{Quote|Mark my words, Raith. Humans are the future.|[[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]] to [[Raith Sienar/Legends|Raith Sienar]]|<ref name="RP" />}}
At the time of the foundation of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], there were several large populist groups active on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] that advocated concepts of Human supremacy, or [[High Human Culture/Legends|Human High Culture]]. These were quickly assimilated into the nascent [[Commission for the Preservation of the New Order/Legends|Commission for the Preservation of the New Order]] (COMPNOR).<ref name="NEC" />

[[File:Rally.jpg|thumb|right|150px|A [[Commission for the Preservation of the New Order/Legends|COMPNOR]] rally, supporting Human High Culture and the Empire's New Order.]]
The tenets of Human High Culture were that Humans were the only truly intelligent and productive members of any society. Believers in this ideology pointed out that it was almost exclusively Humans who had formed and led the Old Republic, and that the Human worlds of the Core were some of the oldest, richest, and most advanced in the galaxy. The contributions of nonhumans were overlooked, with later Imperial propaganda spreading misinformation which claimed such ancient civilizations as the [[Columi/Legends|Columi]] and the [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] were insignificant, recent additions to the [[Galactic community]].<ref name="Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races">''[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races]]''</ref>

As such, through the repealing of such laws as the Rights of Sentience and the creation of new acts, most nonhumans were made second-class citizens. Slavery was re-legalized, with the majority of slaves being nonhumans. Only "pure" works of art (such as operas, [[Holovid/Legends|holovids]], books, etc) were allowed to be produced, viewed, and spread, since only Human culture was worthy enough to be allowed to prosper in the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]]. Non-Humans were "actively discouraged" from participating in government or joining the Imperial military, and Human [[Governor/Legends|governors]] and [[Moff/Legends|moffs]] were placed in command of nonhuman worlds and sectors.

Later in the Imperial era, an anti-Human organization known as the [[Alien Combine]] was formed as a result of the injustices inflicted. However, since the Alien Combine was unwilling to take drastic actions (terrorism), it was wiped out by the Empire.<ref name="X-wing: Wedge's Gamble">''[[X-Wing: Wedge's Gamble]]''</ref>

Despite this, there were many Humans who opposed the Empire's policies, most notably [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]], [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Prestor Organa]], his adopted daughter [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia]], [[Jan Dodonna/Legends|Jan Dodonna]] and [[Garm Bel Iblis/Legends|Garm Bel Iblis]]. These individuals, along with notable nonhumans like [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Gial Ackbar]], and [[Borsk Fey'lya]], founded and led the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], or Rebel Alliance. One of the main principles of the Alliance was the reversal of the Empire's discriminatory policies, and the liberation of enslaved species.<ref name="Rebel Alliance Sourcebook">''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''</ref>

===New Republic and Galactic Alliance===
{{Quote|We have one true enemy: the New Republic, the humans...those who would deny us our rights as sentient beings.|Nolaa Tarkona|<ref name="JB" />}}
[[File:Pellaeon-Gavrisom_Treaty1.jpg|thumb|left|175px|Humans and non-Humans meeting as equals to end the Galactic Civil War.]]

Following the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], the Empire splintered into various warring states. The Rebel Alliance became known as the [[Alliance of Free Planets]] and eventually the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], the new dominant Galactic government. However, the outbreak of the deadly [[Krytos virus]], which affected only nonhumans, following the [[Liberation of Coruscant (Galactic Civil War)|liberation]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] in [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]] drove a wedge between the New Republic's Human and alien populations. This would be resolved when the New Republic acquired [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]] from [[Thyferra/Legends|Thyferra]] following the [[Bacta War]]. Though the New Republic reversed the Empire's discriminatory policies and gave power to oppressed nonhuman species, three of the six [[Chief of State (New Republic)/Legends|Chiefs of State]] who led the New Republic were Human: Mon Mothma, Leia Organa Solo, and [[Cal Omas]].

The views of Human High Culture were still kept alive in the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] for years after the Empire's defeat, by fringe groups such as the [[Human League]] which initiated the [[Corellian Crisis|First Corellian Insurrection]] in [[18 ABY/Legends|18 ABY]]. Slavery of aliens also continued in remote parts of the galaxy and some Imperial [[Fortress world/Legends|fortress worlds]]. In [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]], Admiral [[Natasi Daala|Daala]] strongly weakened this concept within the [[United Warlord Fleets]] by allowing aliens of all kinds to join the Imperial military.

[[File:Humans_of_the_Battle_of_Coruscant.jpg|thumb|250px|Key Human figures of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] [[Talon Karrde]], [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]], Leia Organa and [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] in [[29 ABY/Legends|29 ABY]].]]

After the signing of the [[Pellaeon–Gavrisom Treaty|Bastion Accords]] in [[19 ABY/Legends|19 ABY]] which ended the war between the New Republic and the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]], the fanatical anti-Human [[Diversity Alliance]] attempted to destroy all Humans in retaliation for the oppression inflicted by the Empire. However, their uprising was stopped as soon as it had begun by the Jedi and the New Republic in [[24 ABY/Legends|24 ABY]]. Following the collapse of the Diversity Alliance, the [[Cooperative Council of Independent Planetary Governments]] was formed to promote cooperation between the species of the New Republic.

During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] ([[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]]&ndash;[[30 ABY/Legends|30 ABY]]), the various species and governments of the galaxy were forced to unite to defeat the invasion of the extragalactic [[Yuuzhan Vong]]. In the war's aftermath, the New Republic was reorganized into the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]]. Under Cal Omas, the former government's policies of cooperation between Humans and nonhumans continued.

The [[Second Galactic Civil War]] which started in [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]] created an upsurge of anti-Corellian feeling even amongst their fellow Humans. On Coruscant, Corellians were regarded with suspicion by fellow citizens and many were interned including those who had fought for the Galactic Alliance and its predecessors.

===New Empire and Sith Order===
[[File:Legacybattle1.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Humans continued to play a major role in galactic history during the [[Legacy era]].]]
Throughout the [[Legacy era]], Humans would dominate much of galactic society though the Galactic Alliance's policies of interspecies cooperation would presumably continue. Between [[130 ABY]] and [[137 ABY]], the Galactic Alliance, the Jedi Order and the Yuuzhan Vong [[shaper caste]] initiated a [[Ossus Project|successful terraforming]] of the war-devastated world of [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]] which had been a great Jedi center of learning in the distant past.

As a result, about one hundred devastated worlds turned to the Yuuzhan Vong and Jedi for help. The results proved beneficial for the inhabitants and it seemed that there would be peace in the galaxy. Alas, the [[One Sith|new Sith Order]] under the leadership of [[Darth Krayt]] sabotaged the project by causing mutations and diseases in life forms. The Sith had successfully used the galaxy's dormant prejudice towards the Yuuzhan Vong.

An enraged galaxy turned their fury on the Yuuzhan Vong, Jedi and the Alliance, just as the Sith had wanted. The Galactic Alliance had supported this beneficial terraforming under the encouragement of the New Jedi Order, and found itself facing a secession movement with this deadly new development. This movement was led by the former Imperial Remnant which had by then become the [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|new Galactic Empire]]. Unlike the Humanocentric Galactic Empire of Palpatine, this new Empire treated Humans and aliens more equally. This was evident by its military forces including the legendary [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] having specialized armor created for nonhumanoid species.<ref name="Star Wars: Legacy 3: Broken, Part 3">[[Legacy (2006) 3|''Legacy'' (2006) 3]]</ref> But command positions in the Empire were still apparently reserved for Humans and Near-Humans like the [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]]. The Sith, on the other hand, had only few Humans among the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]] of their Order.<ref name="Star Wars: Legacy 1: Broken, Part 1">[[Legacy (2006) 1|''Legacy'' (2006) 1]]</ref>

Eventually, the [[Council of Moffs/Legends|Moff Council]] (which controlled the Empire) invoked the [[Treaty of Anaxes]] and declared war on the Galactic Alliance. Many of the dissatisfied worlds defected from the Alliance to the Empire, with others declaring their neutrality. It was at this time the new Sith Order made itself known, proposing an alliance with the Empire after contacting [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Morrigan Corde|Nyna Calixte]], [[Director of Imperial Intelligence]].

The resulting [[Sith–Imperial War]] lasted three years, during which Imperial forces reconquered Coruscant and absorbed the remainder of the Alliance into the Empire. The Jedi were forced to retreat to their [[Jedi Academy (Ossus)|temple]] on [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]], which was later the focus of an [[Massacre at Ossus|attack]] by Sith forces led by Darth Krayt and Imperial forces led by Moff [[Rulf Yage]]. Shortly after, the Sith turned against Emperor [[Roan Fel]] and his [[Imperial Knight]]s.

==Near-Humans==
[[File:Jerec.jpg|thumb|right|150px|[[Yun]] (an [[Epicanthix]]) and [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Jerec]] (a [[Miraluka/Legends|Miraluka]]).]]
{{Main|Near-Human}}
Many species in the galaxy appeared to be very closely related to Humans, as they shared many physical traits. These were described as being [[near-Human]], and were believed to have descended from Humans that evolved along distinct lines on other worlds. Among the most prominent near-Human races were the [[Chalactan/Legends|Chalactans]], the [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]], the [[Hapan]]s, the [[Kiffar/Legends|Kiffar]], the [[Miraluka/Legends|Miraluka]], the [[Mirialan/Legends|Mirialans]], the [[Zeltron/Legends|Zeltrons]], and the [[Umbaran/Legends|Umbarans]]. All of these were mostly Human in appearance, but had unique and distinct defining characteristics. Often, the biological differences were small enough that Humans and near-Humans could interbreed. In many cases, it was difficult to tell whether a given population represented a distinct species, or merely a race or ethnic group of baseline Humans.

The term near-Human was more specific than [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]]. While near-Humans were biologically related to Humans, other humanoid species merely shared broad external similarities such as an upright bipedal posture.

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Silver, longitudinal beings who wavered on two points and spoke in a high-pitched gibberish that reminded us of Mocking Trees.|[[Etro Edthatt|Etro]] and [[Droza Edthatt]]'s description of Humans|<ref name="MaA">''[[Monsters and Aliens from George Lucas]]''</ref>}}
The origin of Humans in ''[[Star Wars]]'' is unknown (though many in the galaxy believe that they originated on Coruscant). A canceled, and therefore non-canon, novel known as ''[[Alien Exodus]]'' would have explained the origins of Humanity and their connection with Earth, but it was never published for a variety of reasons. The storyline in this novel involved both space travel and [[Time travel/Legends|time travel]], which would have explained the line "A long time ago, in a galaxy far, far away."

Though Humans have been portrayed in film mostly by actors of European descent, Humans in the ''Star Wars'' galaxy appear to be ethnically diverse. Specific physical features are rarely associated with specific Human groups; however, most known [[Serroco]]ans appear to possess [[Wikipedia:epicanthal fold|epicanthal folds]], while [[Socorro/Legends|Socorroans]] have generally dark skin.

Leland Chee indicated that during the Legends Expanded Universe, the humans lived longer largely because they didn't have to take into account the actors getting older, although by the time of the [[Canon]] Expanded Universe, he stated that humans lived the same average lifespan as humans in the real world.<ref name="Canon age span">{{Twitter|HolocronKeeper|status/783493608989003776|[[Leland Chee]]|quote=@MaxN2100 Similar to real-world. Was easier to say they lived longer in Legends because we didn't have to account for actors getting older.|archivedate=20190722080534}}</ref>
